newsitem.title: ITALY: Port sealed off after wartime bomb found in Naples.
newsitem.headline: Port sealed off after wartime bomb found in Naples.

text.p: The central port of Naples was closed on Sunday and dozens of roads around the area were sealed off after workers discovered an unexploded bomb dating from World War Two, police said.
Some 150 families living near the site were evacuated as army experts worked to defuse the American bomb.
A semi-circular wall of rubber tyres, five metres high (16 feet) and some 25 metres (yards) long, was constructed around the bomb as a precaution to limit damage to the area if the device exploded.
The bomb was discovered during work to enlarge the port in the Sant'Erasmo area, close to the centre of the southern Italian city.
Naples was pounded by the United States airforce in the early 1940s as Allied forces sought to drive the fascist powers north. Thousands of people died in the raids.
Police said they did not expect the bomb disposal team to complete its work before evening and until then no boats were allowed to anchor in the harbour.
